text: You've got your ticket, your destination booked, and your perfect carry-on packed. You're ready to fly.
Then, at the check-in counter, reality hits: your bag is too big, or you have a second one. That used to be free, right?
It feels like a sneaky trick, pure greed. Why not just bake the cost into the ticket price like before?
But the system is smarter: it's called 'unbundling'. By stripping out extras, the base ticket price looks much lower.
This lets airlines capture two kinds of customers: those who only want the cheapest possible ticket, and those willing to pay for convenience.
So next time you pay for that bag, remember: you're not being scammed. You're simply buying the features you need, from a menu designed just for you.
